name: BrickColor
simple: A BrickColor is a color picked from Roblox's fixed list of named colors, like "Bright red", "Lime green", or "Pastel Blue". Each one has a name and a number. It is the older, simpler way to color parts. For any exact color you want, use Color3 instead.
analogy: BrickColor is like a box of crayons with a set number of colors, each with a name printed on it. Color3 is like a paint mixer where you can make any shade.
whenToUse: Coloring a part by a friendly name, like BrickColor.new("Really red")
Picking a random color from the list with BrickColor.random()
Checking a team's color, since Team.TeamColor is a BrickColor
Matching a part to the palette shown in Studio's color picker
where: Works in any script on the server or client. Make one with BrickColor.new, BrickColor.palette, BrickColor.random, or shortcuts like BrickColor.Red().

terms.named color: One of the colors in Roblox's built-in list, each with an exact name like "Bright blue".
terms.Number: Every BrickColor has an ID number. For example "Pastel Blue" is number 11.
terms.palette: A grid of 128 BrickColors, the same ones shown in Studio's BrickColor picker. Palette spots are numbered 0 to 127.
terms.Color3: The more flexible color type that can be any mix of red, green, and blue.
terms.read-only: You can look at the value but not change it.

examples.title: Color a part three different ways
examples.code:
local part = Instance.new("Part")
part.Anchored = true
part.Position = Vector3.new(0, 5, 0)
part.Parent = workspace

part.BrickColor = BrickColor.new("Really red") -- by name
task.wait(1)
part.BrickColor = BrickColor.new(11)           -- by number (Pastel Blue)
task.wait(1)
part.BrickColor = BrickColor.random()          -- a surprise color
print(part.BrickColor.Name)
explain: We make an anchored part so it floats in place.
BrickColor.new("Really red") picks a color by its exact name.
BrickColor.new(11) picks by number. 11 is Pastel Blue.
BrickColor.random() picks a random color from the 128-color palette, and we print its name.

examples.title: Turn a part a random color when touched
examples.place: Script inside a Part in Workspace
examples.code:
local part = script.Parent

part.Touched:Connect(function(otherPart)
	-- Only react to players, not other parts
	local humanoid = otherPart.Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if humanoid then
		part.BrickColor = BrickColor.random()
	end
end)
explain: script.Parent is the part this Script is inside.
Touched fires whenever something bumps the part.
We check for a Humanoid so only characters change the color.
BrickColor.random() gives a new random named color.

gotchas: Names must match exactly, including spaces and capitals. If the name is wrong, you silently get "Medium stone grey" instead of an error.
BrickColor only has a fixed list of colors. If you need an exact shade, use part.Color with a Color3.
BrickColor.palette(n) errors if n is not between 0 and 127.

BrickColor.new.simple: Makes a BrickColor. You can give it a name ("Bright red"), an ID number (11), three numbers from 0 to 1 for red, green, blue, or a Color3. With colors, it finds the closest named color in the list. If the name or number does not exist, you get "Medium stone grey".
BrickColor.new.example:
local byName = BrickColor.new("Pastel Blue")
local byNumber = BrickColor.new(11)               -- also Pastel Blue
local byRGB = BrickColor.new(0.502, 0.734, 0.859) -- closest match: Pastel Blue
local byColor3 = BrickColor.new(Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0)) -- closest to pure red
print(byName, byNumber, byRGB)
BrickColor.new.gotcha: A typo in the name gives gray, not an error. Print the result if a color looks wrong.

BrickColor.palette.simple: Makes a BrickColor from its spot in the 128-color palette (the grid in Studio's color picker). Spots go from 0 to 127.
BrickColor.palette.gotcha: Numbers outside 0 to 127 throw an error.

BrickColor.random.simple: Gives a random BrickColor from the 128-color palette. Each call can give a different one.
BrickColor.random.example:
local part = workspace:FindFirstChild("Part")
if part then
	part.BrickColor = BrickColor.random()
end

BrickColor.White.simple: A shortcut that gives the "White" BrickColor.
BrickColor.White.example:
local part = Instance.new("Part")
part.BrickColor = BrickColor.White()
part.Parent = workspace

BrickColor.Gray.simple: A shortcut that gives "Medium stone grey", the default gray. It is also what you get when a name or number is not found.

BrickColor.DarkGray.simple: A shortcut that gives the "Dark stone grey" BrickColor.

BrickColor.Black.simple: A shortcut that gives the "Black" BrickColor.

BrickColor.Red.simple: A shortcut that gives the "Bright red" BrickColor.

BrickColor.Yellow.simple: A shortcut that gives the "Bright yellow" BrickColor.

BrickColor.Green.simple: A shortcut that gives the "Dark green" BrickColor. Note it is dark green, not bright green.

BrickColor.Blue.simple: A shortcut that gives the "Bright blue" BrickColor.

BrickColor.Number.simple: The ID number of this BrickColor, the same number you can pass to BrickColor.new. Read-only.

BrickColor.r.simple: How much red is in this BrickColor, from 0 to 1. Same as .Color.R. Read-only.

BrickColor.g.simple: How much green is in this BrickColor, from 0 to 1. Same as .Color.G. Read-only.

BrickColor.b.simple: How much blue is in this BrickColor, from 0 to 1. Same as .Color.B. Read-only.

BrickColor.Name.simple: The name of this BrickColor, like "Pastel Blue". It is the same text you can give to BrickColor.new. Read-only.
BrickColor.Name.example:
local c = BrickColor.random()
print("You got: " .. c.Name)

BrickColor.Color.simple: The same color as a Color3. Use it when something needs a Color3, like a GUI background, but you started with a BrickColor. Read-only.
BrickColor.Color.example:
local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
label.BackgroundColor3 = BrickColor.new("Bright orange").Color
